d5a44ef3-b40f-4a44-907e-a4eb2f38dc56.description: Error ratio over 5m is above 14.4x the 1% error budget (fast burn); at this rate a 30-day budget lasts about 2 days.

facts.statement: Checkout revision 2 was created at 07:33:05Z, about 2.5 minutes before the alert, with the change cause 'payment client moved to port 9999'.
The only pod-template difference between checkout revisions 1 and 2 is PAYMENT_ADDR, changed from payment:8080 to payment:9999.

Checkout's error spans are all PaymentService/Charge gRPC dial failures ('dial tcp 10.96.101.68:9999: i/o timeout'), propagated as 'failed to charge card' through PlaceOrder, frontend and frontend-proxy HTTP 500s.
Payment has one revision (06:45:29Z), is 1/1 available, and had no changes or Warning events in the incident window.
Payment's logs and spans stop at 07:33:04 and it has no error logs in the last 30 minutes. Payment's server-side Charge rate was 0 at 07:36.
All 18 flagd flags are off, and the only Warning events in otel-demo are readiness-probe failures on other services around 06:45-06:46.
Checkout's SLI error ratio peaked at 0.65 at 07:09, dropped to 0 around 07:13-07:20, and was back at 0.38 at 07:35.
Product-catalog's own server-side GetProduct p95 peaked at 9530 ms at 07:21 and recovered by 07:36, with mostly UNSET (not ERROR) statuses.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Run kubectl get svc payment -o yaml and check the payment container ports; check that checkout's live PAYMENT_ADDR env matches revision 2.
hypotheses.statement: Payment's Service and container expose only port 8080, so nothing listens on 9999 and the dial times out.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check NetworkPolicies in otel-demo; test a connection from the checkout pod to payment:9999 and payment:8080.
hypotheses.statement: A NetworkPolicy or similar blocks checkout-to-payment traffic on 9999, which would explain i/o timeout rather than connection refused.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Pull payment logs and traces for 07:00-07:15 and check for flag or deployment events in that window.
hypotheses.statement: The 07:03-07:12 payment Charge error wave came from a transient payment-side fault unrelated to the current incident.

inferences.statement: Checkout's revision 2 is the most likely cause of the current error burn. Checkout started dialing payment:9999 at 07:33:05 and the failures began right after, while payment (not changed) stopped seeing traffic at 07:33:04.
Checkout's own pod shows no crash or restart events, so the fault is configuration and not checkout's pod health.

root_causes.cause: Revision 2 changed PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:9999 (the only config change). Checkout's Charge dials to 10.96.101.68:9999 time out, and checkout surfaces these as failed charges and HTTP 500s. Payment is likely not listening on 9999 (its port is 8080); this still needs confirming.

A latency problem in product-catalog and its astronomy-db dependency (GetProduct p95 about 9.5 s, astronomy-db p95 about 4.7 s) during 07:19-07:21. It recovered by 07:36 and is not the source of the current checkout errors, so it is a secondary issue.

An unexplained payment-side Charge error wave from 07:03 to 07:12, with no matching payment error logs, flag change or rollout change. It predates checkout revision 2 and stopped on its own, so the cause is unknown.

diagnosis.summary: Checkout's current error burn (about 35% of requests) is most likely caused by its own revision 2 (07:33:05Z), which changed PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999 and was the only pod-template change. Checkout's error spans are PaymentService/Charge dial timeouts to payment:9999, and payment's logs and spans stop at 07:33:04, which fits checkout no longer reaching payment. The earlier payment error wave (07:03-07:12) predates revision 2 and is unexplained. The product-catalog/astronomy-db latency wave (07:19-07:21) has recovered and is secondary. Suggested fix: confirm payment's Service and container ports, then roll checkout back to revision 1 (PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080).

actions.reason: Checkout revision 2 (07:33:05Z, 'payment client moved to port 9999') changed PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999, the only pod-template change. Checkout's errors are PaymentService/Charge dial i/o timeouts to 9999, and payment is unchanged. Reverting to revision 1 restores the working address.

alternatives.why_not: The fault is in the pod template configuration, not a stuck process. A restart would bring up pods with the same PAYMENT_ADDR=9999 and keep failing.
Checkout is not short of capacity. Its failures are dial timeouts to a wrong port, so more replicas would fail the same way.
Not chosen. The rollback is reversible, and the evidence points to the release, so waiting only prolongs the fast burn.

plan.summary: Roll checkout back to revision 1, which restores PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080 and removes the bad port 9999 change from revision 2. Expect checkout's error ratio to fall toward zero within a few minutes as new pods pick up the old config and Charge calls succeed again.
